args.title: deviation-analysis-memo.docx
args.body:
DEVIATION ANALYSIS MEMORANDUM
Senior Secured Credit Facility Term Sheet — Counterparty (Lender) Markup

TO:      Deal Team / Engagement Partner
FROM:    Banking & Finance Associate
RE:      Counterparty Markup Deviation Analysis — Senior Secured Credit Facility Term Sheet
DATE:    [Engagement Date]
FILE:    Matter File 3 — Banking Finance
OUTPUT:  deviation-analysis-memo.docx

================================================================================
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
================================================================================

This memorandum compares the lender’s markup of the Senior Secured Credit Facility term sheet against the original firm-standard term sheet (base materials), and reconciles each deviation against (i) the firm banking-finance playbook posture embedded in the base materials, (ii) the controlling partner instructions in the deal-team correspondence, and (iii) the financial and disclosure data in the schedules and exhibits.

Three material deviation clusters are identified:

  1. Indemnification economics — silent reduction of the indemnification cap, and conversion of the basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.
  2. Material Adverse Effect (MAE) — new carve-outs for regulatory action of the type already at issue on this matter.
  3. Survival / limitation period — shortened survival for core representations, in direct conflict with Exhibit B.

Controlling partner instruction (latest message in the deal correspondence): the client will CONCEDE the basket conversion, but treats ANY survival-period reduction as a WALK-AWAY issue. Earlier messages stating the opposite priority ordering are superseded and are not followed.

Primary recommendation: accept the basket conversion; reject the survival-period reduction as a walk-away; push back hard on the silent indemnification-cap reduction and the MAE regulatory carve-outs in light of Schedule 3.7 and Schedule 5.2; require the survival matrix in Exhibit B to control.

================================================================================
II. MATERIALS REVIEWED
================================================================================

Operative record (banking-finance matter):

  A. Base materials / original term sheet posture
     — Deal materials — banking-finance analyze: Counterparty Markup Deviation
       Analysis of Senior Secured Credit Facility Term Sheet (Matter File 3)
     — Firm-standard provisions on representations and warranties, covenants,
       conditions to closing, indemnification, and termination; playbook-aligned
       baseline for indemnification structure, MAE definition, and survival.

  B. Lender / counterparty markup
     — Counterparty markup — banking-finance (same related shape)
     — Deviations flagged: indemnification cap reduction; deductible→tipping
       basket; MAE regulatory carve-outs; shortened survival for core reps.

  C. Schedules and exhibits (financial / disclosure data)
     — Schedule 3.7 — two pending regulatory inquiries intersecting the markup’s
       MAE carve-outs.
     — Schedule 5.2 — retained liabilities that the markup’s indemnification
       changes would silently shift.
     — Exhibit B — survival matrix that the markup’s limitation-period change
       contradicts.
     — Governing rule: scheduled exceptions control over general statements in
       the base banking-finance materials.

  D. Partner instructions (deal-team correspondence)
     — Latest message REVISES priorities: concede basket conversion; survival-
       period reduction is walk-away.
     — Earlier messages with opposite priority ordering are NON-CONTROLLING.

  E. Excluded
     — Unrelated administrative correspondence (distractor / misfiled). Not
       relied upon.

Cross-references applied: playbook baseline (base materials), partner
instructions (latest controlling message), and financial/disclosure data
(Schedules 3.7 and 5.2; Exhibit B).

================================================================================
III. PLAYBOOK AND BASELINE POSITION (ORIGINAL TERM SHEET)
================================================================================

Under the original term sheet and firm banking-finance playbook posture reflected in the base materials:

  • Indemnification cap: full firm-standard cap (not reduced). Cap is a
    negotiated economic term; silent reductions are non-market from the
    borrower/sponsor protective perspective and require express client consent.

  • Basket: structured as a deductible (true deductible). Losses below the
    basket do not aggregate to open the full claim once the threshold is
    crossed.

  • MAE: standard definition without carve-outs for the specific category of
    regulatory action implicated by this facility and the disclosed inquiries.

  • Survival: core representations survive for the periods set in Exhibit B
    (survival matrix). Limitation periods in the body of the term sheet /
    credit documentation must conform to Exhibit B; Exhibit B controls in the
    event of conflict.

  • Disclosure hierarchy: scheduled exceptions qualify and narrow the related
    representations; they control over general statements in the base
    materials. Markup changes that interact with scheduled items must be
    read together with those schedules, not in isolation.

================================================================================
IV. DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 1 — Indemnification Cap (Silent Reduction)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Markup change:
  The lender’s markup silently reduces the indemnification cap relative to the
  original term sheet / firm-standard cap.

Baseline / playbook:
  Firm-standard cap retained unless expressly renegotiated with client
  authority. Silent reductions are a red-flag economic concession.

Financial / schedule cross-reference:
  Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities. A reduced cap, read together with
  Schedule 5.2, would silently shift residual exposure on those retained
  liabilities onto the client once the lowered cap is exhausted. The economic
  effect is not limited to “ordinary” indemnity claims; it interacts directly
  with scheduled retained liabilities.
